subject: Science
central_question: How can temperature be measured reliably and safely for the human body, laboratory substances and the surrounding air?
in_scope_units: Testing whether the sense of touch can reliably distinguish hot and cold
Defining temperature and identifying thermometers as measuring devices
Using digital clinical thermometers safely to measure body temperature
Understanding normal body temperature and the Celsius, Fahrenheit and Kelvin scales
Observing the construction, range and smallest division of a laboratory thermometer
Following the correct procedure for measuring a liquid's temperature
Comparing readings of boiling water and recognising sources of measurement difference
Recording maximum and minimum air temperature and understanding weather observations
Applying temperature concepts in the chapter-end exercises
banned_topics: Detailed heat transfer by conduction, convection and radiation
Medical diagnosis or treatment based only on thermometer readings

known_pitfalls.claim: Touch always tells us correctly which object is hotter.
known_pitfalls.correction: The same tap water can feel warm to one hand and cool to the other, so touch is not always reliable.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every healthy person must have a body temperature of exactly 37.0 °C.
known_pitfalls.correction: 37.0 °C is an average normal temperature; a healthy person's reading may vary slightly with age, time of day and activity.

known_pitfalls.claim: A clinical thermometer can be used for boiling water.
known_pitfalls.correction: Boiling water lies outside the clinical thermometer's intended range; a suitable laboratory thermometer is required.

known_pitfalls.claim: A laboratory thermometer should be removed before its reading is taken.
known_pitfalls.correction: Its reading must be taken while the bulb remains immersed because the liquid column begins to fall after removal.

recommended_example_progression: Compare prediction and observation to establish that touch is unreliable.
Measure body temperature and interpret the common temperature scales.
Find range and smallest division of a laboratory thermometer.
Compare, record and analyse temperature data.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Refer to the chapter-end section 'Let us enhance our learning', Questions 1-14, followed by the 'Learning further' investigations.
